narrative:
Axel Springer National Media & Tech (int-nmt, Intigriti) was a three-pass clean-negative engagement run on 2026-05-21. Secrets (Pass A/B/C) found 0 verified credentials across the axelspringer GitHub org (68 repos, full trufflehog scan, 22s) and 3 cloned repos from codesearch; all 7 noseyparker matches were false positives — env-var placeholder text, a developer test fixture with phone-number data in a `.rest` file, and a bcrypt hash in a README documentation example. Buckets found 12 s3scanner-flagged candidates out of 80 scanned (20 brand bases); all 12 returned AccessDenied on the mandatory list-objects-v2 recheck, marking the 7th consecutive engagement confirming s3scanner's ACL flags are a structural false positive. The takeovers pass enumerated 331 subdomains (seed cap 3; sub cap 100) and found 95/100 bearing CNAME chains — the highest CNAME rate recorded — with 0 dangling endpoints.

Two structural FP patterns in the secrets pass are worth codifying. The noseyparker Generic Password detector fired twice on `denniskern/swerve` README documentation: a bcrypt hash example used to illustrate password hashing in a tutorial is not a credential. It also fired twice on `codetipster/oudioo` because a `.rest` HTTP test fixture contained a Nigerian phone number and placeholder passwords in a test user definition. Both are recurring FP shapes — README bcrypt examples and `.rest` test fixture data — that will appear again in future engagements. A `noseyparker_path_skip` rule on `.rest` files (Generic Password hits only from fixture data) and a README.md bcrypt-hash pattern would eliminate these without touching real signal. Confidence is low for a single engagement; both patterns are sufficiently distinct and low-risk to codify at low confidence now.

The takeovers pass surfaced a novel structural pattern: hub-and-spoke CNAME delegation. Axel Springer runs two large CNAME hubs: `swerve.bild.de` (34 bild.de promo/campaign subdomains all CNAME to it, Bild's internal redirect mesh) and `schneevonmorgen.com` (57 welt.de subdomains all CNAME to it, the Damoh third-party ad-injection platform). Neither hub is dangling — both resolve to live, claimed services. The current takeover-hunter pipeline correctly returned 0 candidates after subzy found 0 VULNERABLE entries, so no false-positive report was generated. However, if either hub ever went temporarily unresolvable (domain expiry, DNS propagation gap), all 91 spoke subdomains would simultaneously appear dangling to any scanner. The `cname_hub_skip` rule for these two specific targets would prevent noise if the pattern recurs; both entries are low-confidence observations from a single engagement and should be treated as informational until corroborated.

The codesearch noise issue — `bild` and `politico` base names generating 30+ dork hits each because `bild` is German for 'picture' and `The-Politico` is the US news org's GitHub handle — is best handled as a narrative note rather than a hard rule. The current pipeline correctly handled it (repos cloned by codesearch signal returned 0 trufflehog hits, and the selection heuristic chose infrastructure-adjacent repos not brand-name-noise repos), so the FP didn't produce a false positive. A general `codesearch_noise_skip` rule for common-word base names would need more careful design (it could suppress real signal on future engagements where the target happens to own a common-word org). This remains narrative-only for now.

For the next run against int-nmt: the strict cap of 100 subdomains left 231 subdomains from the welt.de/bild.de/politico.eu corpus unscanned. The 25-wildcard scope makes this a high-surface takeover target — consider running a second pass with a higher sub cap or splitting into per-seed runs. The `axelspringer` GH org is clean and well-managed; Pass A's 22s full-org scan confirms it's not a ticking-secrets target. Bucket hunting is structurally unproductive for this org (bare brand names like `bild`, `petbook`, `techbook`, `travelbook`, `stylebook`, `fitbook` are extremely generic — most are occupied by unrelated parties at AccessDenied). If revisiting, prioritise takeover surface expansion over bucket re-scans.
